summary: Focused retest of iteration_2 HIGH issue (/api/edge/overnight contract mismatch) + regression sweep + cookie auth sanity. Backend: 32/32 pytest PASS (tightened test_overnight to enforce the normalized contract: verdicts + detail, each verdict has symbol/verdict/best_session=OVERNIGHT/best_direction/best_oos_t_stat/p_value/bh_significant/mtc_robust). Curl probe confirmed verdicts=9, detail=18, run_id present, best_session uniformly 'OVERNIGHT'. Frontend e2e (network-aware Playwright via external HTTPS): login -> Edge Lab -> Overnight tab -> RUN -> awaited /api/edge/overnight 200 -> [data-testid='edge-verdicts-table'] rendered 9 rows AND [data-testid='edge-detail-table'] rendered 18 rows. Regression: Session Scan (2 verdicts rendered) and NY Conditional (2 verdicts rendered) still work. Cookie auth sanity: document.cookie does NOT expose access_token (HttpOnly intact); logout redirects to /login and a subsequent visit to /edge-lab is bounced back to /login. No React pageerrors; only expected 401 console log when /api/auth/me probes a logged-out session. The iteration_2 HIGH issue is RESOLVED.
critical_code_review_comments: analysis.py::_normalize_overnight is a clean, minimal adapter: picks best leg per symbol by oos_t_stat, derives direction from leg string, sets best_session='OVERNIGHT', preserves raw rows under result['detail']. Idempotent (no-op when upstream already returns 'verdicts', e.g., mock_data path). KEEP rule matches frontend expectation (mtc_robust OR oos_t_stat>=1.8).

EdgeLab.jsx now correctly reads result?.detail for the secondary table (was the prior gap). Both tables share the same testids across tabs, so per-tab schemas should keep the column definitions stable — currently good.
Backend test test_overnight previously accepted 'rows' OR 'verdicts' to flag the regression; tightened in this iteration to enforce only the normalized contract (verdicts + detail). Still passes.
Pytest still uses xdist (LoadScopeScheduling) — 32 tests in ~40s against the live external API; acceptable. No flakies observed.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 2's HIGH issue (Overnight tab empty due to upstream 'rows' vs frontend 'verdicts' mismatch) is fully resolved by backend _normalize_overnight in analysis.py and the EdgeLab.jsx detail-table integration. Backend pytest is 32/32 with the strict normalized-contract assertions now in place. All edge tabs render rows. Cookie auth (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax) remains intact end-to-end on the external HTTPS preview URL. The external cloudflare-tunneled API returns more rows than the requested 'symbols' filter for /api/edge/overnight (~9 verdicts / ~18 legs) — that is the upstream behavior, not a bug.
rca of the issue: RCA from iter_2: external upstream /api/edge/overnight returned only 'rows' (dense per-leg) while session-scan/ny-conditional returned aggregated 'verdicts'. Frontend EdgeLab.jsx rendered (result?.verdicts || []), so the Overnight tab showed an empty table. Mitigation applied (and verified here): backend analysis.py::_normalize_overnight synthesizes 'verdicts' by selecting the best leg per symbol (by oos_t_stat) and exposes the raw rows under 'detail'. KEEP rule = mtc_robust OR oos_t_stat>=1.8. This restores a single uniform contract across all three edge endpoints. Curl + Playwright network-and-DOM verification both confirm: status=200, verdicts populated, detail populated, UI tables render rows.
